title: 9. Bull vs. Bear, Portfolio Action & Redeployment Plan
book_title: Chapter 9: Bull vs. Bear, Likely Outcomes & Our Action Plan

epigraph.quote: Conviction is not the absence of a bear case; it is knowing exactly which bear-case trigger would prove you wrong—and pricing the position so you survive if it happens.
epigraph.author: Institutional Risk & Capital Allocation Principle

web_blocks.html: Our business audit gives LLY a COMPOUNDER_PASS and a PASS on all six KPIs. The Reverse DCF sets a $1,660 Base value, and the Stage 2 tape is CAP_WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT at $1,382.75 CMP. Next, we weigh both sides before locking our final verdict and capital plan.

Good risk control starts before the first buy order. The S&P 500 sits in a Downtrend with eight distribution days, so we do not go all-in on day one. Instead, we wait for $1,283.94–$1,323.04 support and hold 50% in T-Bills for a dip into $1,283.94–$1,323.04. That two-step plan lifts reward-to-risk from 1.24:1 at CMP to 2.05:1 at support. It also caps downside with a strict $1,158.45 weekly-close stop.

web_blocks.caption: Steelman Bull vs. Skeptic Bear Debate — Evidence-Weighed Assessment
rows: +53% Q3 2026 volume growth and Medicare Bridge (>500k Rx, ~70% LLY share) expand TAM far faster than price cuts.
-15% Q3 2026 realized price erosion accelerates toward -20%+ under IRA/Medicare/TrumpRx negotiations and payer pushback.
Volume wins near-term; monitor realized price delta quarterly as key thesis guardrail.
Foundayo (orforglipron, FDA approved Apr 2026) opens needle-averse primary care; retatrutide (Q1 2027 BLA) widens efficacy moat.
Novo Nordisk oral Wegovy, Amgen MariTide, Roche, and compounders fragment obesity share and cap long-term pricing power.
Lilly holds the strongest multi-modal incretin stack (injectable + small-molecule oral + triple agonist).
>$50B U.S. manufacturing buildout creates an insurmountable supply moat and converts to 75%+ FCF/NI as plants mature in 2027–2029.
Heavy $7.8B–$10B+ annual capex + $42.5B gross debt keeps trailing P/FCF at 64.9x and leaves little margin for demand hiccups.
Growth capex is backed by 31.6% ROIC; FCF inflection is a timing issue, not a solvency issue.
26.75x Forward P/E (0.79 PEG) is reasonable for 33.8% 5Y EPS growth; Stage 2 pullback to +6.70% above 10W EMA is buyable.
44.5x trailing P/E and 15.3x EV/Sales leave de-rating risk (like NVO's 11.4x Fwd P/E) if growth decelerates in a Downtrend market.
Staged entry (50% CMP, 50% $1,284–$1,323) with $1,158.45 hard stop controls downside.
web_blocks.takeaway: The Bull case rests on verifiable volume (+53%), pipeline approvals (Foundayo), and 31.6% ROIC; the Bear case centers on net price erosion (-15%) and valuation de-rating risk.

book_paragraphs: We have reached the moment of truth. Over the past eight chapters, you and I have audited Eli Lilly's century-and-a-half evolution, dissected its four therapeutic segments, traced $100 of revenue down to free cash flow, stress-tested its manufacturing moat, graded management's promises against delivery, priced its Reverse DCF at $1,382.75, and read its Stage 2 chart.

Now let's put the Bull and Bear cases in the same room and force an honest decision. The Bull case is grounded in hard operational facts: +53% volume growth in Q3 2026, over 500,000 prescriptions already flowing through the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program with Lilly capturing ~70% of new starts, Foundayo's April 2026 FDA approval opening the oral primary-care market, and a 31.6% return on invested capital that justifies its $50 billion manufacturing buildout.

The Bear case is equally clear and deserves respect: realized net prices fell 15% in Q3 2026, and if government negotiations or rival launches (from Novo Nordisk, Amgen, or Roche) push annual price erosion past 20%, or if $7.8B–$10B annual capex delays free cash flow recovery, a 44.5x trailing P/E stock can de-rate sharply—just as Novo Nordisk compressed to 11.4x forward earnings.

book_subsections.title: Probability-Weighted Outcomes & Our Earned Verdict
paragraphs: Weighting those scenarios—25% Bull ($1,920), 55% Base ($1,660), and 20% Bear ($1,040)—yields a 12-to-18-month expected value of $1,601.00 (+15.78%). Against our hard invalidation stop at $1,158.45, the Base target of $1,660.00 delivers 1.24-to-1 reward-to-risk right at today's $1,382.75 price, and 2.05-to-1 if we catch the $1,283.94–$1,323.04 support zone.

Because Lilly earned a Compounder Pass on business quality, a Pass on all six leading KPIs, and Clear for Consideration on its Stage 2 tape, we do not hedge timidly. Our New-Capital Verdict is Wait for Support (Tier 1, Core Alpha). However, because the broader S&P 500 is in a Downtrend with eight distribution days, we hold 100% cash and wait for a pullback into the $1,283.94–$1,323.04 support zone (2.05:1 R:R).

book_subsections.title: Current Holding Audit & 100% Capital Redeployment
paragraphs: Checking the November 18, 2026 consolidated US brokerage ledger across Charles Schwab and Robinhood, Eli Lilly is currently Not Held (0 shares, 0 shares to sell). For the next marginal unit of US equity capital, our 100%-reconciled plan retains 100% in USD Cash while waiting for LLY's $1,283.94–$1,323.04 support zone (0% at CMP), and allocates 0% to outside peer Amgen ($440.66, 1.40:1 asymmetry), which fails to match Lilly's ROIC or growth runway.

book_subsections.title: Why We Hold 50% Cash Alongside Tranche 1
paragraphs: Some readers might ask: if Eli Lilly passes every business, KPI, valuation, and Stage 2 check, why not put 100% of the allocation to work today at $1,382.75? The answer lies in respecting market-regime discipline. As of November 18, 2026, the broader S&P 500 sits in a Downtrend with only 44.4% of stocks above their 50-day moving average and eight institutional distribution days logged in the past 25 sessions. Even the strongest Stage 2 leaders can experience sharp, sympathetic pullbacks of 5% to 8% when index-level liquidity tightens.

By deploying 50% into LLY Tranche 1 at $1,382.75 and holding 50% in USD Cash earning T-bill yields, we achieve two goals simultaneously: we capture immediate exposure to a 0.79-PEG compounder before any upside breakout above $1,475.25 leaves us behind, and we keep dry powder ready to buy Tranche 2 at a superior 2.05-to-1 reward-to-risk ratio if index weakness nudges LLY into the $1,283.94–$1,323.04 10-week EMA zone. And if the thesis or market breaks entirely, our $1,158.45 weekly-close stop caps portfolio damage.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good investing is rarely all-or-nothing heroics. Buying half of a Tier-1 Stage 2 compounder at 26.8x forward earnings while keeping half your cash ready at the 10-week EMA—and a hard stop at $1,158.45—lets you participate in upside without surrendering discipline to a Downtrend tape.
